quickAnswer: Groton has one of the newer housing stocks around: only 39.3% of homes predate 1980 (47th of 50 for old homes), yet 56.1% still burn oil and 9.9% use bottled gas (ACS 2022). Its electric utility is municipal, which changes the heat pump rebate path.
body: ## A newer-built town that still runs on delivered fuel

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) counts 3,801 housing units in Groton and gives the town a median build year of 1987, newer than the 1975 of the middle town. Just 1,495 homes (39.3%) were built before 1980, which puts Groton 47th of the 50 towns we serve on that measure. The biggest single group, 1,549 units (40.8%), went up between 1980 and 1999.

Fuel oil or kerosene heats 2,080 occupied homes (56.1%), which puts Groton 14th of 50 for oil, with the middle town at 36.5%. The town also counts 3,801 housing units in all. Bottled or tank (LP) gas heats 366 (9.9%), 5th-highest. Utility gas heats 785 homes (21.2%), and electricity only 224 (6.0%), 46th of 50.

Replacement decisions here often revolve around delivered fuel. A boiler or furnace from the 1980s can be near the end of a normal service life, and the real question is often whether to renew an oil or LP system or move to a heat pump.
## Old Groton, still in the numbers

The newer majority does not mean there is no old housing. 702 homes (18.5%) date from 1939 or earlier, 20th of the 50 towns, and 350 more are from 1940 to 1959. Groton has a long record: it was settled and incorporated in 1655, and on March 13, 1676, during King Philip's War, all its buildings except four garrisons were raided and burned. Lawrence Academy at Groton was founded in 1793 and Groton School in 1884.

Early Groton also had industry. Miners found a large soapstone quarry in 1828, the Hollingsworth family acquired a paper mill in West Groton in the early 1800s, and railroad lines reached South Groton in the 1840s. One of those lines survives as the MBTA Fitchburg Line. Ayer split off in 1871. The town was named for Groton in Suffolk, England, and as The Plantation of Groton it first included all of present-day Groton and Ayer and almost all of Pepperell and Shirley. By 1790 it was the second-largest town in Middlesex County, with 1,840 residents.
## The municipal electric department and your rebate path

Groton is served by the Groton Electric Light Department, a municipal utility. That matters. Municipal electric service changes the rebate picture: Mass Save heat pump money generally follows only homes that burn natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor, and the rest look to the department's own program. Because only 21.2% of Groton homes use utility gas, the municipal program is likely to be the path for most households, and even a gas home depends on whether the gas comes from a Mass Save sponsor. Ask the electric department what it offers before ordering equipment, and see the [heat pump page](/cities/groton/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
## Who lives in what

Single-family detached houses make up 3,104 units (81.7%), against 76.7% for the middle town. 195 units are attached townhouses, 202 are in two-family buildings and 230 are in buildings of 5 or more units. Renters hold 455 households (12.3%). Groton is described as an affluent bedroom community roughly 45 miles from Boston; the median home value is $628,500. Vacancy is 2.4% (91 of 3,801 units), 37th of 50. Route 2 and the MBTA Fitchburg Line connect the town loosely to Boston.

faq.q: Do Mass Save heat pump rebates apply in Groton?
faq.a: Possibly, but probably not for most homes. Groton Electric Light Department is a municipal utility, so Mass Save rebates generally go only to homes on natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor. Everyone else turns to the department's own program. Check with the electric department and masssave.com before you buy.

faq.q: My Groton house is newer than 1980. Does it still need a heating load assessment?
faq.a: Yes. Most Groton homes are newer, but their needs still depend on size, windows, insulation and layout. We assess the home's heating load before quoting any system, so the equipment is neither oversized nor undersized, whatever the build year.

faq.q: Should I stay with oil or switch when my Groton boiler fails?
faq.a: It depends on the house and your plans. Oil heats 56.1% of Groton homes and LP another 9.9%, so a like-for-like replacement is a common option. A heat pump, with or without the old boiler kept for backup, is the other route. A written estimate comes at no cost.

faq.q: Is gas available on my street in Groton?
faq.a: Only 21.2% of homes use utility gas, so many addresses may not have a main. The gas company can tell you whether one runs past your house. Where no main passes the house, the options are oil, LP or a heat pump. Ask the gas company first, since only it can confirm a main.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Oil heats 56.1% of Groton homes, with LP and utility gas behind (ACS 2022), and the median home dates from 1987. A replacement often involves a decision about the fuel, not just the unit. Utility gas serves 785 homes, 39th of 50.
body: ## Replacing a boiler or furnace in a late-1980s town

The median Groton home dates from 1987, newer than most of the 50 towns. A heating system that fails in a house of that age can be an original unit near the end of a normal service life, which makes the choice of fuel and system the main question.
### The fuel question

Oil is the dominant fuel here, LP gas ranks 5th-highest among our 50 towns, and utility gas is the minority fuel. If a gas main runs past the house, conversion is possible. If not, the choices are a new oil or LP system, a heat pump or a combination. The gas company can confirm main availability.
### What matters in a replacement

- The fuel, tank and its condition.
- The distribution system: baseboard, radiators or ducts.
- Venting and the chimney or flue.
- The home's heating load, so the replacement is the right size for the house as it is now.
### Gas permits
Gas jobs go through a licensed plumber or gas fitter, who pulls the permit. Ask the building department which inspection follows.
### The fuel numbers

Delivered fuel dominates: LP gas heats 366 homes (9.9%), wood heats 101 (2.7%), and the Census lists 154 homes under other fuel or coal, on top of the oil count above. A replacement that stays on delivered fuel keeps the tank in play, while a heat pump moves some of the load onto electricity, which heats only 224 homes (6.0%) now.
### Rental properties

Groton has 455 renter households (12.3%) and 202 units in two-family buildings. The State Sanitary Code sets a floor of 68 F by day and 64 F at night for rented units during the heating season. Heat is the landlord's cost unless the lease says otherwise. This is general information, not legal advice.
### Emergencies

Call (508) 786-8755 at any hour. A person answers emergency calls day and night, and the estimate you get is written and free. If you want to compare with a heat pump, the [heat pump page](/cities/groton/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers the Groton rebate picture.

faq.q: Is my older boiler worth repairing?
faq.a: It depends on the fault and the unit's condition. A single failed part on a boiler that is otherwise sound can be repaired. A cracked heat exchanger or a long list of repairs points to replacement.

faq.q: Can I add a heat pump without removing the oil system?
faq.a: Yes. A heat pump can carry much of the load while the oil system stays as backup. We assess the home first to decide how much capacity to add.

faq.q: What if my Groton house runs on LP gas?
faq.a: LP gas heats 366 homes (9.9%), 5th highest of the 50 towns. A replacement can stay on LP or move to a heat pump, and the tank, burner and venting are looked at as part of the quote.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Groton is 81.7% detached houses, with 5.1% attached townhouses and 13.2% in multi-unit buildings. Detached houses often take central air, while apartments and additions can suit ductless heads.
body: ## Cooling detached houses, townhouses and small buildings

Detached houses lead the mix in Groton, but the town still has several layouts. The ACS counts 195 attached townhouses, 202 units in two-family buildings and 70 in buildings of 3 or 4 units. Each type cools differently, and the ACS counts no mobile homes in town. The 757 units built in 2000 or later (19.9%) are generally tighter than older houses, which makes sizing matter more.
### Houses with ducts

Where a house has ducts, the question is whether they are sized and sealed for cooling. A duct system laid out for winter heat may not move enough air for summer cooling, so airflow gets checked along with the condenser.
### Houses without ducts

Many older homes were built without central air, and Groton has 702 units from 1939 or earlier and 350 from 1940 to 1959. A house heated by a hot-water boiler often has no ducts. A ductless mini-split can cool it with an indoor head per room or zone and a small line set to an outdoor unit.
### How Groton compares

Groton ranks 18th of 50 for detached homes, at 81.7% against 76.7% in the middle town, and 32nd for homes in multi-unit buildings (13.2%, or 502 units). The largest age band is 1980 to 1999 with 1,549 units (40.8%), and 317 homes date from 2010 or later. A median build year of 1987 puts Groton 47th of 50 on the oldest-first list, so a good share of cooling jobs here involve equipment from the newer half of the stock.
### Electricity is the minor heating fuel
Electric heat is rare here (46th of 50), so adding a large cooling load can be a significant electrical change for a house. Panel capacity should be checked before a big unit is ordered.
### Apartments and additions
A ductless system is a practical option for a unit in a small building or a room added to a house, because it avoids opening walls for ducts.
### Humidity and size

A unit that is too big cools rooms quickly, then stops before the air has dried; sizing from the house avoids that short cycling. See the [maintenance page](/cities/groton/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) for seasonal checks.

faq.q: Can I add cooling to a Groton house with a hot-water boiler?
faq.a: Yes. Ductless heads connect to the outdoor unit by a slim line set, so a hot-water house needs no new ducts. The rooms to be cooled set the capacity, and the condenser needs a clear spot outside.

faq.q: Is a mini-split good for a finished room over the garage?
faq.a: Often yes, since such a room can be hard to reach with ducts. A single head can handle one area, subject to a load calculation.

faq.q: Can a heat pump replace my air conditioner?
faq.a: Yes. A heat pump cools as well as heats, so it can take over from a failing air conditioner in the same job. Our heat pump page covers the heating side.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Groton is served by Groton Electric Light Department, a municipal utility, so the Mass Save path is narrow and the department's own program matters. Oil heats 56.1% of homes and LP gas another 9.9%, so the question comes up often.
body: ## A municipal utility in a tank-fed town

Oil heats 2,080 Groton homes (56.1%, 14th of 50) and LP gas heats 366 (9.9%, 5th of 50). Utility gas reaches 785 (21.2%), and electricity heats 224 (6.0%), 46th of 50. A heat pump swaps delivered fuel for electricity, and cold-climate models are built for New England winters.
### Who pays what

Groton Electric Light Department is municipal. The standard Mass Save heat pump rebate generally goes only to homes heated by natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor, and the gas homes number 785 at most. For everyone else the department's own program is the place to ask, and we do not know what it pays. Where Mass Save does apply, the whole-home rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500, after weatherization; the terms are in our [heat pump overview](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Age bands against the weatherization test

The 757 homes from 2000 on (19.9%) meet the age test directly, and 317 of them date from 2010. The rest begin with a Home Energy Assessment: 1,549 homes from 1980 to 1999 (40.8%), 702 from 1939 or earlier, 443 from 1960 to 1979 and 350 from 1940 to 1959. Groton's median home dates from 1987, so a larger share of houses than in most towns has a chance of passing on age alone.
### Where the equipment fits

With 3,104 detached houses (81.7%) there is generally room for outdoor equipment. The 202 two-unit homes and 230 units in buildings of 5 or more raise shared-wall and electrical questions. Ductless heads suit baseboard and radiator houses, and a ducted unit can reuse sound ducts. Electric heat is rare here, so a new heat pump can mean new load on the panel, which gets checked before anything is ordered.
### The boiler stays or goes

A boiler can remain for the coldest days, with the heat pump doing the rest. The heating-load assessment decides how much capacity is needed, and a home on LP gas, which is 5th highest in the 50 towns here, goes through the same step as one on oil. Our [heating page](/cities/groton/heating-installation-repair) covers the straight replacement.

faq.q: Who do I ask about a rebate in Groton?
faq.a: Start with Groton Electric Light Department, then check masssave.com. The path depends on how your home heats today and which utility serves it.

faq.q: Is a house from the 1987 median good for a heat pump?
faq.a: Groton's median home dates to 1987 (ACS 2022), newer than most of the 50 towns, but age alone does not decide. Insulation, heating load and the weatherization step matter more.

faq.q: Can a heat pump run beside the oil boiler?
faq.a: Yes. The two can share the work, with the boiler covering the coldest days. We assess the heating load first to decide how much heat pump capacity to add.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Oil is the main heating fuel in Groton, and oil burners need a yearly cleaning. A tune-up can also show whether a system of any age has years left or is due for planned replacement.
body: ## Tune-ups when the equipment is in its middle age

The largest age band in town is 1980 to 1999, with 1,549 units. A tune-up can show whether equipment of any age has years left. For oil: a yearly cleaning, nozzle and filter change and combustion check. For LP and gas: burner, venting and controls. For heat pumps: coils, filters and refrigerant-side checks.
### The fuel mix

Oil heats 2,080 Groton homes (56.1%), utility gas 785 (21.2%), LP gas 366 (9.9%), electricity 224 (6.0%) and wood 101 (2.7%), with 154 homes on other fuel or coal. Each fuel has its own burner, venting and controls, so the yearly visit is different for each. LP ranks 5th of the 50 towns.
### Catching decline early

An aging system does not always fail suddenly. Rising bills, new noises, more cycling and uneven rooms are warnings. A tune-up can bring them to light early, which leaves time to plan a replacement before a cold night forces one.
### Age of the stock

Groton's median home dates to 1987, and it is 47th of 50 for homes built before 1980 (39.3%). Even so, 702 homes date from 1939 or earlier, and the 1,549 homes from 1980 to 1999 now carry equipment that may be many years old. A tune-up gives each of them a reading on condition.
### Rentals

The town has some rental housing, and 230 units are in buildings of 5 or more units. Owners occupy 3,255 of 3,710 homes (87.7%), so most service decisions rest with the owner. Landlords who service heating before winter can lower the risk of a cold-snap failure, which affects every tenant at once.
### Seasonal rhythm

- **September or October:** heating tune-up.
- **April or May:** cooling and mini-split check.
- **Any time:** noises, odors or soot are reasons to call early.
### What owners can do

Change filters on schedule, keep outdoor units clear of leaves and snow, keep the burner area clean and clear, and check thermostat settings. Know where the shutoff for your fuel is, and keep the oil or LP supply from running low in a cold week. A tank that runs dry can leave air in an oil line, which may then need a service call to restart.
### When you call
Have the fuel, how old the unit is, anything on the nameplate and what you noticed ready. For cooling see the [cooling page](/cities/groton/air-conditioning-installation-repair).

faq.q: How often should an oil system be serviced?
faq.a: Annually, in early fall. A skipped cleaning can leave soot behind and cost efficiency.

faq.q: Is a tune-up useful on a system under 20 years old?
faq.a: Usually. Even a younger system has filters, drains and outdoor coils that need care, and a small problem is often cheaper when it is found early.

faq.q: Do wood stoves need a yearly check?
faq.a: Yes. Wood heats 101 Groton homes (2.7%), and a stove or fireplace insert needs its chimney inspected and cleaned by a qualified chimney sweep. We look at the heating equipment and controls around it.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Groton's housing is mostly from 1980 on, which usually means tighter houses than older ones. Humidity, ventilation and combustion safety are the main air questions, along with the oldest houses in town.
body: ## Air in houses built after 1980

Most of Groton's housing was built from 1980 on. Houses from that period are generally tighter than older ones, which saves energy and keeps moisture, cooking fumes and chemicals from furnishings inside unless ventilation moves them out.
### Ventilation first

A bath fan that vents outside, a range hood that does the same and regular filter changes help in any house. In a tight house, a fresh-air ventilation system can be worth discussing, because it brings in outdoor air on a controlled path instead of relying on gaps. Filters matter too: a higher-rated filter catches more dust and pollen but can also restrict airflow, so the system has to be checked before one is fitted.
### The older minority

Some Groton houses date from 1939 or earlier: 702 units, or 18.5%, 20th of 50. Gaps in older shells can let in dust, pollen and damp air while diluting other pollutants, and a qualified specialist should test for older materials ahead of any renovation.
### What the age bands say

Housing from 1980 to 1999 is the biggest group at 1,549 units, with 757 more from 2000 on. Construction of those decades tends to be tighter, and the median year of 1987 sits in that stretch, which leaves a bigger share of Groton's air quality to depend on fans, filters and fresh-air paths.
### Combustion safety

With oil heating 2,080 homes, LP 366 and wood 101, burners and stoves are common, so carbon monoxide alarms near sleeping areas matter. Burners should be tuned and flues kept clear, which a yearly service covers. Soot near a burner or a stained flue is a sign to call early, since either can point to poor combustion or venting.
### Humidity

Dry winter air gives way to damp summers, and both reach indoor spaces. A damp basement calls for a dehumidifier plus a repair to whatever lets the water in. If a humidifier is run in winter, it helps to watch for condensation on windows, which can be a sign that the air holds more moisture than the house can handle.
### What we can do

- Upgrade filtration and keep filters changed.
- Add a humidifier or dehumidifier tied to the system.
- Add or fix ventilation.
- Clean ducts that are visibly dirty or damaged.

faq.q: Is a newer house better for air quality?
faq.a: Not automatically. A tighter house needs ventilation to work properly. Older houses leak more but may carry older materials.

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Not automatically. Visible dirt, mold or damage is the reason to clean ducts. We inspect the system first.

faq.q: Do two-family and larger buildings share air?
faq.a: The Census counts 202 units in two-family buildings and 230 in buildings with 5 or more units. Where homes share walls, cooking smells, moisture and fumes can move between them, so ventilation and sealing are checked building by building, since one unit's habits can reach its neighbors. A short walk-through of the building usually shows where air is likely to travel.
